title: vLLM
description: The agent works with a model on your vLLM server instead of the cloud: only the server's address is opened, nothing else.

de.title: vLLM
de.description: Der Agent arbeitet mit einem Modell auf Ihrem vLLM-Server statt in der Cloud: nur die Adresse des Servers ist offen, sonst nichts.

llm.label: vLLM server (sandbox-ai llm list), NAME or NAME:MODEL
llm.hint: sandbox-ai llm add vllm --kind vllm --url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --model MODEL

notes: Register it once: sandbox-ai llm add vllm --kind vllm --url http://127.0.0.1:8000 (another address, --api-key-secret SECRET for a key, --vpn PROFILE for a server behind a VPN).
Start it with: vllm serve MODEL --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser PARSER (the parser of the model's family, e.g. hermes or qwen3_coder).
OpenCode works with any vLLM; Codex needs vLLM 0.10.0 or later (streamed tool calls 0.18.0), Claude Code 0.11.1 or later (Anthropic Messages API).

A GPU server elsewhere: sandbox-ai llm add gpu --kind vllm --url https://gpu.example.org:8443 --api-key-secret GPU_KEY, or http://100.x.y.z:8000 --vpn ts behind Tailscale; --llm gpu then brings its VPN along.

NAME:MODEL picks a model (sandbox-ai llm models NAME lists them); without it the server's default (llm add --model) or its only one. sandbox-ai llm check NAME --agent AGENT asks the server whether it has the API that agent needs.

On this host's loopback (http://127.0.0.1:PORT) only with Podman: sandbox-ai opens that one port for the sandbox, and the server must listen on 127.0.0.1. In your LAN or tailnet: a private address, or https.
The agent reaches nothing but the server (--no-provider-defaults): no cloud provider, its login is not copied in; the server's key stays with the connection proxy.
